entries.title: Operation Wolf
entries.summary: Taito's NES version of its 1987 arcade rail shooter: commando Roy Adams fights through six stages to rescue five hostages.
entries.why_it_matters: The arcade original popularised military light-gun rail shooters. The NES version supports the Zapper.
entries.gameplay_notes: Shoot the quota of soldiers and vehicles in each stage. Ammo and grenades are limited; restock by shooting items. Shoot down incoming projectiles, and avoid hitting nurses and civilians. The NES version has multiple endings depending on how many hostages you save.

entries.content_notes: Playable with the NES Zapper or a controller.

entries.title: Overlord

entries.title: Pac-Mania

entries.gameplay_notes: Four mazes: Block Town, Pac-Man's Park, Sandbox Land and Jungly Steps. Jump over most ghosts, but later Funky and Spunky can jump too. Red pellets double ghost points and green pellets add speed. Dawdle and your jump weakens.

entries.title: Pirates!
entries.summary: Rare's NES port, published by Ultra Games, of Sid Meier's 1987 open-world Caribbean adventure: sail as a privateer or pirate for Spain, England, France or the Netherlands between 1560 and 1680.
entries.why_it_matters: Sid Meier's first game with his name in the title: an open-ended game with no fixed ending.
